headline: Quiet, steadying session: SBP's MPC held the policy rate at 11.5% as expected (87.5% of surveyed analysts called it correctly) — no surprise, no real market shock. Bigger driver was Friday's late rally: KSE-100 actually closed Sep 11 UP 0.98% at 170,511.85 (not the ~13:39 PKT pre-close snapshot of 168,865.04 used in that review) after Gulf-Iran talks in Oman over Strait of Hormuz shipping lifted sentiment into the close. Today the index is giving a little of that back, off ~0.62% to ~169,453 as of this review, with Brent still elevated near $102.5/bbl but not spiking further. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.05M, P/L ~-Rs 203,600 (~-1.99% on cost) — actually a bit BETTER than the ~-2.29% shown three reviews ago, since Friday's real close was a recovery, not a crash. No holding moved more than ~3% since the last review; nothing new stock-specific. AVN's EXIT call remains unexecuted (holdings unchanged in index.html) and AICF/MICF still show their pre-redeployment balances, so treat last review's dry-powder redeployment as still pending too, if it wasn't done off-app already.
market: KSE-100: Friday Sep 11 actually closed at 170,511.85, UP 1,646.81pts (+0.98%) — a late-session reversal driven by news that Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers would meet their Iranian counterpart (via Oman mediation) to discuss a temporary arrangement for managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. That means the prior review's logged close (168,865.04, -1.79%) was a pre-close data snapshot, not the real close — the actual day was a recovery, not a fresh leg down. Today, Monday Sep 14: SBP's Monetary Policy Committee met as scheduled and held the policy rate unchanged at 11.5% (unanimous), the base case that 87.5% of a pre-meeting AHL survey expected. SBP noted FX reserves now above the $18bn end-June target and a recent S&P sovereign upgrade to 'B', against CPI inflation running ~10.18% in FY27's first two months — a genuinely mixed but non-alarming picture, and the rate hold removes one source of uncertainty this review cycle. Separately, the Oman-mediated Hormuz talks appear to be continuing rather than collapsing, which is the more consequential thread for markets than the rate decision itself. Brent crude sits ~$102.5/bbl (+2.5% on the day) — elevated but not accelerating into fresh panic. As of this review (~14:30 PKT, roughly an hour before close) the KSE-100 is trading around 169,453, down ~1,059pts (-0.62%) from Friday's real close — a normal give-back, not a new selloff. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is ~10.6%, still past the 10% dry-powder trigger crossed three reviews ago but not deepening toward the 15% heavier-redeployment threshold. AVN: no new company news since the H1 FY26 loss filing; still down heavily and the EXIT call is now unexecuted across many consecutive reviews. EFERT: no new Q3 results or fresh dividend announcement; the Sep 3 payment (Aug 10 ex-date) remains the last confirmed one. DRAP pharma pricing review: still unresolved, no change since early September. DATA QUALITY: stock prices in this review come from prices.json refreshed at 2026-09-14T09:37:59Z (~14:37 PKT, essentially current) fetched directly via raw.githubusercontent.com since git access to github.com's main host is still blocked from this session (see note 9). Fund NAVs remain frozen at Aug 13 — now 32 days stale.

entries.basis: Monthly-timeframe accumulation zones for a 10-25yr horizon: where fundamentals + monthly support align to add in small portions. 'entry' = start nibbling at/below; 'add' = deeper monthly support to load more. Pakistan macro-aware (SBP 11.5%, KSE-100 off the Jan ATH). These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.
